Function graphs

Source: R/functions_graph.R
function_graphs.Rd

ParametricFunction() traces a curve t -> c(x(t), y(t), z(t)). FunctionGraph() plots y = f(x) in scene coordinates across the frame. ImplicitFunction() draws the zero set of f(x, y).

Usage

ParametricFunction(
  func,
  t_range = c(0, 1),
  scaling = LinearBase(),
  dt = 1e-08,
  discontinuities = NULL,
  use_smoothing = TRUE,
  use_vectorized = FALSE,
  ...
)

FunctionGraph(func, x_range = NULL, color = PURE_YELLOW, ...)

ImplicitFunction(
  func,
  x_range = NULL,
  y_range = NULL,
  min_depth = 5,
  max_quads = 1500,
  use_smoothing = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

func

For ParametricFunction(), a function of t returning 2 or 3 coordinates. For ImplicitFunction(), a function of x and y.

t_range

c(t_min, t_max, t_step); the step defaults to 0.01.

scaling

Scale applied to the sampled t values; see LinearBase().

dt

Gap left on each side of a discontinuity.

discontinuities

Values of t where the curve is broken.

use_smoothing

Whether to smooth the sampled polyline.

use_vectorized

Whether func accepts a vector of t values. Like upstream, it must then return coordinate rows: a 2 x n or 3 x n matrix such as rbind(cos(t), sin(t), 0), or list(x, y) or list(x, y, z). A matrix with one point per row is accepted only when its shape cannot be read as coordinate rows.

...

Passed to VMobject().

x_range, y_range

Ranges of the variables.

color

Color.

min_depth, max_quads

The implicit curve is traced on a grid of cells that are split min_depth times everywhere and then further where the function changes sign, up to max_quads cells (the adaptive method of the isosurfaces Python package, as upstream).

Value

A mobject.

Details

The point function of a graph is stored in the field func (upstream calls it function, a reserved word in R); get_function() returns it.

Examples

ParametricFunction(function(t) c(sin(2 * t), sin(3 * t), 0), t_range = c(0, TAU))
#> <ParametricFunction> 2516 points, 0 submobjects
FunctionGraph(cos, color = RED)
#> <FunctionGraph> 5692 points, 0 submobjects
ImplicitFunction(function(x, y) x^2 + y^2 - 4)
#> <ImplicitFunction> 2784 points, 0 submobjects
